title: Write-Blockers: Read-Only by Hardware
description: A write-blocker is a hardware bridge between an analyst's workstation and a suspect drive that passes read commands and blocks every write command — physically enforcing read-only access during forensic imaging. Tableau and WiebeTech make the known bridges. The evidence drive cannot be altered through the blocker, which is the point.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Why Forensics Needs Them
description: Digital forensics must prove the evidence was not altered: imaging a drive through a write-blocker with hash verification before and after is the standard that makes the image admissible. Booting a suspect drive without one can change timestamps and destroy evidence. The blocker is the chain of custody's first link.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: How Blocking Works: Command Filtering
description: Write-blockers filter at the storage protocol level — ATA, SCSI, USB mass storage, NVMe — dropping or rejecting write opcodes while translating reads. Some also block the HPA/DCO hidden-area commands that could conceal data. Filtering happens in hardware/firmware the host cannot override.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Tableau TX1 and Forensic Bridges
description: The Tableau TX1 is the iconic forensic bridge: multi-interface (SATA, USB, IDE, PCIe) imaging with built-in hash verification and a touchscreen workflow. One device images almost any drive forensically. It is the standard field tool the industry recognizes.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Hash-Verified Imaging
description: Forensic imaging copies every sector and hashes the source and the image — matching SHA-256 means the copy is bit-identical. The hash is recorded in the case file as the integrity proof. Verification is not optional; it is the evidence.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: NIST CFTT Validation
description: NIST's Computer Forensics Tool Testing program validates write-blockers: the tool must block all modifying commands across interfaces and the tests are published. CFTT reports are how labs choose blockers. Tested tools, not trusted claims.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: NVMe and Modern Interfaces
description: NVMe drives need NVMe-aware blockers — the protocol differs from SATA and so does the filtering. M.2, U.2, and PCIe add-in cards each need the right bridge. The blocker must match the evidence's interface or there is no acquisition.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: USB Write-Blockers
description: USB write-blockers sit between the workstation and USB drives, filtering mass-storage writes — the quick tool for thumb drives and externals in triage. Same principle, smaller package. Triage moves fast; the blocker keeps it honest.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Network and Remote Acquisition
description: Some suites acquire over the network with software write-blocking agents — useful for live enterprise collection where pulling drives is impractical. Hardware blockers remain the gold standard for dead drives. The method follows the situation.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Write-Blocked Booting (Live Preview)
description: Analysts sometimes boot a suspect drive read-only through a blocker for a live preview — seeing the system without changing it. Every write the OS attempts gets blocked and logged. Preview informs the full imaging plan.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: HPA and DCO Hidden Areas
description: Drives can hide areas — Host Protected Area and Device Configuration Overlay — that normal reads skip; forensic blockers and tools address these so hidden data is still acquired. What the OS cannot see, the lab still images. Completeness matters.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Chain of Custody Documentation
description: Every acquisition documents drive serial, blocker used, hashes, time, and analyst — the paperwork that carries the image into court. Gaps in documentation are gaps in admissibility. The form is as important as the forensic copy.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Blocker Maintenance and Testing
description: Labs re-test blockers periodically — firmware updates get validated, interfaces get exercised — because a blocker that stopped blocking is worse than none. Test logs join the case files. Trust is maintained, not assumed.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Mobile Device Considerations
description: Phones need their own acquisition discipline — often logical plus physical methods with write-protection where the interface allows. The principle is identical: alter nothing. Mobile forensics is its own specialty with the same ethics.
